bugs: PostController.php:21 — `->when($request->validated('tag'), ...)` treats a tag named "0" as falsy, so `?tag=0` returns every post instead of filtering. A probe confirmed it. impl-2 has the same bug.
PostController.php:31-32 — creating the post and syncing its tags aren't wrapped in a transaction, so a failure while syncing tags leaves a post with only some of its tags (minor).
antipatterns: routes/api.php:7-11 — five hand-written routes with separate PUT and PATCH lines where `Route::apiResource('posts', ...)->except('show')` would do. The likely reason was to attach `->can()` to each route.
StorePostRequest.php:25-28 — a `tagNames()` helper used once and only on the store request. The update path calls `validated('tags')` directly, which is inconsistent.
PostObserver.php:28 — the slug lookup runs one `exists()` query per collision and isn't safe against concurrent requests. The unique index is the only backstop (both impls).
strengths: Very thin controller that uses `$request->user()->posts()->create(...)`, `safe()->except('tags')`, `when()` with `$request->enum()` and `#[Scope]` attribute scopes.
Modern Laravel 12/13 conventions: `#[Fillable]`, `#[ObservedBy]`, `#[Scope]`, a `casts()` method and a backed enum with `Rule::enum`.
Authorization lives in the routes with `->can('update','post')`, so non-owners get 403 before validation runs. Tested, including with an invalid payload.
The policy uses `$post->user()->is($user)`, which needs no query.
Duplicate tag names are quietly de-duplicated, which suits 'created on the fly'. Eager loading uses the `tags:id,name` column subset.
Store returns 201 through the resource's built-in recently-created handling, with no manual status code.

The 26 tests are thorough: guests, mass-assignment protection for slug and user_id, slug collision, tag reuse, keeping existing tags on update and clearing them with an empty array, keeping an existing published_at, non-owner 403, 404, cascade delete of the pivot, filters (alone and combined), pagination including the default size of 15, and query validation with exact messages.
Factories carry `@use HasFactory<...>` generics and a `published()` state.

bugs: PostController.php:35 — `->when($request->validated('tag'), ...)` ignores a tag named "0", so `?tag=0` returns every post. A probe confirmed it (same as impl-1).

StorePostRequest.php:21 / UpdatePostRequest.php:21 — the `distinct` rule rejects `['php','php']` with a 422 instead of creating tags on the fly. This was deliberate and tested, but it's less forgiving than the task implies.
PostController.php:45-46 — creating the post and syncing its tags aren't in a transaction (minor).
antipatterns: PostController.php:48 — `PostResource::make(...)->response()->setStatusCode(Response::HTTP_CREATED)` is unneeded ceremony. A resource wrapping a recently created model already returns 201, and the change forces the return type to JsonResponse.

PostController.php:17-28 — `HasMiddleware` with string `can:update,post` middleware in the controller splits route authorization away from the routes file. `Route::...->can()` or a `Gate::authorize` call is more direct.
AppServiceProvider.php:23 — adds a global `Model::shouldBeStrict()`, which changes app-wide behaviour beyond the task's scope.
Post.php:50 — `trim($name)` duplicates the TrimStrings middleware, and the `distinct` rule makes the later `->unique()` dead code.
PostController.php:37 — `paginate($request->validated('per_page', 15))` passes a raw string from the query. `$request->integer()` is cleaner (it works only because the paginator casts the value).
PostController.php:33 — `with('tags')` loads full tag rows when only the names are output (minor).
strengths: Has the same modern model attributes as impl-1 (`#[Fillable]`, `#[ObservedBy]`, `#[Scope]`), a `casts()` method, an enum with `Rule::enum`, and Form Requests for index, store and update.
The observer handles slug generation and setting published_at, and the policy uses `user()->is()`.

Tests cover the main paths: guests, non-owner 403 with an invalid payload, 404, keeping tags on update and clearing them with an empty array, keeping an existing published_at, combined filters, pagination and validation. They use the `hasTags()` magic factory method.

v.rationale:
I ran `php artisan test` on both: all 26 tests pass in impl-1 and all 19 pass in impl-2. The two are nearly identical in structure: same enum, the same observer for slugs and published_at, the same `#[Scope]` scopes, the same policy, the same migration and the same Form Requests. Neither installed Sanctum, so the `auth` middleware with `actingAs` is correct for both.

They share one bug, which a probe confirmed: `when($request->validated('tag'))` treats a tag named "0" as empty and skips the filter. That makes the differences between them decisive.

impl-2 adds needless ceremony:
- It sets the 201 status by hand, which the resource already does.
- It moves `can:` middleware into the controller with `HasMiddleware` instead of keeping it on the routes.
- It switches on `Model::shouldBeStrict` for the whole app, which is out of scope.
- It trims tag names twice.
- It passes `per_page` as a raw string instead of using `$request->integer()`.
- It rejects duplicate tag names with a 422 instead of de-duplicating them, which is less forgiving than 'created on the fly' suggests.

impl-1 is slightly leaner throughout. It quietly de-duplicates tags, loads only the tag columns it needs, keeps authorization in the routes with `->can()`, and has a clearly stronger test suite: mass-assignment protection, the default page size, exact validation messages and filter combinations. impl-1's hand-written routes are its main idiom weakness. impl-1 ranks first.
